title: Unrestricted admission filled the CPU cache but slowed serving
summary: Removing the frequency gate filled the CPU cache, but throughput fell 4.58% for ARC and 11.86% for prefetch. More admitted bytes and more cache activity did not establish useful capacity.
scope: Four fresh Qwen3-4B dense BF16 runs, 45 requests each, 1,440 MiB GPU KV and 448 MiB CPU KV. Thresholds 2 and 0 were compared with ARC retention in both policies; all 180 requests passed exactness and transfer checks.
limitations: One run per arm in fixed order; closed-loop schedules and observer volume differ. Eleven admitted blocks at threshold 2 became 4,781/4,962 store events at threshold 0. No constrained semantic ranking occurred, and allocation peaks included startup.
decision: Retain admission as a cost control. The proposed bounded consecutive-prefix write policy was a design, not a tested win; CPU copies do not themselves release native GPU references.

chart.caption: Single fixed-order observations, no uncertainty interval. Negative is slower.
